title: Consequences of environmental change

match.reason: The closest bank point, Human-induced environmental change, covers the types of change (pollution, biodiversity loss, degradation) rather than the consequences the new point needs, such as extreme weather and harm to livelihoods, so no existing point teaches this idea.

draft.title: Consequences of environmental change
card: Environmental change can have effects that last a long time. It can harm other living things and people.
Biodiversity is the variety of living things in an area. When a habitat, the place where a species lives, is cleared or damaged, species can decline or disappear.
Soil can lose nutrients or wash away. Water can become polluted or too salty to use. This is called degradation.

Some changes can lead to more extreme weather, such as hotter heatwaves. Livelihoods are the ways people earn a living, such as farming and fishing. They can be harmed when soil, water or fish stocks decline.
draft.remember: Environmental change can cause habitat and biodiversity loss, degraded soil and water, extreme weather and harm to livelihoods.

a.q: A wetland is drained for farmland, and many of the frog and bird species that lived there disappear. What is this a consequence of?
opts: More extreme weather in the region
a.why: The wetland was the place where the frogs and birds lived, so draining it removed their habitat. The species then declined, which is a loss of biodiversity. Nothing in the case describes soil, weather or income, so those options do not fit.
a.clue: Where did the frogs and birds live?

b.q: Poor farming leaves bare paddocks near Narrabri, and rain washes the topsoil into a creek. Which pair of consequences does this describe?
opts: Loss of habitat and extreme weather
Harm to livelihoods and extreme weather
Degraded water and loss of biodiversity
b.why: Topsoil washing away means the soil is degraded. The soil that ends up in the creek makes the water degraded too. The other pairs include extreme weather or biodiversity loss, which the case does not describe.
b.clue: Think about what is lost from the paddock and what ends up in the creek.
